stories.hook: ¿Qué porcentaje de depresivos muestra inflamación sistémica?
stories.headline: Un cuarto de pacientes con depresión presentan CRP >3 mg/L, indicando fenotipo inflamatorio
stories.finding: Los autores revisan estudios humanos y encuentran que aproximadamente el 25 % de los pacientes con depresión tienen niveles de proteína C‑reactiva superiores a 3 mg/L, lo que respalda la existencia de un fenotipo inflamatorio. Señalan que los tratamientos antiinflamatorios solo muestran beneficios consistentes en pacientes seleccionados mediante biomarcadores.
stories.takeaway: Este dato sugiere que una proporción significativa de pacientes podría beneficiarse de estrategias terapéuticas dirigidas a la inflamación, lo que justifica la incorporación de pruebas de CRP en la evaluación clínica y el diseño de ensayos estratificados.
stories.paperTitle: Neuroinflammation in Major Depressive Disorder: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Implications
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is heterogeneous, and low-grade systemic inflammation may contribute to illness in a clinically relevant subgroup. Methods: This narrative review examined human studies published between January 2010 and June 2026, prioritizing systematic reviews, meta-analyses, cohort studies, central biomarker research, and randomized trials. Results: Approximately one-quarter of patients with depression have CRP levels above 3 mg/L, supporting an inflammatory phenotype rather than a universal inflammatory model. Immune signals may affect brain function through blood–brain barrier, neural, neurovascular, and metabolic pathways, influencing neurotransmission, stress regulation, oxidative balance, and neuroplasticity. CRP is the most accessible clinical marker, but no biomarker reliably identifies inflammatory depression. Anti-inflammatory treatments show inconsistent benefits, with the strongest signals observed in biomarker-selected patients. Conclusion: Inflammation contributes to MDD in some patients, but single-marker diagnosis and routine anti-inflammatory treatment are not currently justified. Biomarker-stratified trials are needed to develop precision therapies.

stories.headline: Journaling de autocompasión reduce el malestar de la rumiación
stories.finding: En un estudio experimental con 15 participantes, se compararon tres tipos de escritura: reflexión centrada en afecto negativo, reflexión autocompasiva de afecto positivo y reencuadre cognitivo. Los modelos mixtos mostraron que la condición de autocompasión disminuyó significativamente el malestar emocional respecto a la reflexión negativa.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que incorporar ejercicios de autocompasión en intervenciones de rumiación puede atenuar el sufrimiento emocional, ofreciendo una estrategia breve y factible para mejorar la regulación afectiva en pacientes con pensamiento repetitivo negativo.
stories.paperTitle: Shifting the Emotional Impact of Repetitive Negative Thinking: Effects of Self- Compassion and Reappraisal Journaling
stories.journal: Digital Access to Scholarship at Harvard (DASH) (Harvard University)
stories.originalAbstract: Repetitive Negative Thinking (RNT) is commonly associated with maladaptive psychological outcomes characterized by intrusive, perseverative thought patterns. Across literature, self-compassion has repeatedly been identified as a protective factor, and theoretical models of repetitive thought (RT) suggest that its outcomes depend on the mode of engagement rather than the mere presence of RT themselves. The present study investigated whether a self-compassionate reflection influences the emotional responses to RNT within a process-focused framework amid continued RT. Fifteen participants completed a brief within-subjects online journaling task involving three conditions: negative affect–focused reflection (NA-SC), positive affect self-compassion reflection (PA-SC), and cognitive reappraisal. Emotional distress (Subjective Units of Distress Scale; SUDS) and perceived thought negativity were assessed following each condition, and state RNT (RTQ-10) and state self-compassion (SCS-SF) measures were assessed at baseline, and following the NA-SC and PA-SC conditions. Mixed-effects models for repeated measures indicated a significant effect of journaling condition on emotional distress, F(2, 28) = 22.25, p .0001, with distress highest following NA-SC (M = 48.0), lower following PA-SC (M = 33.3), and lowest following reappraisal (M = 26.0). Perceived thought negativity also differed across conditions, F(2, 28) = 7.72, p = .0021, whereas state RNT levels did not significantly change (p = .1986). State self-compassion increased during PA-SC relative to NA-SC, F(1, 14) = 6.71, p = .021. Findings suggest that modifying how individuals engage with RT may lead to reductions of emotional consequences without reducing thought frequency, supporting process-oriented models of RT.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué evitamos lo que nos causa ansiedad?
stories.headline: Nueva clasificación de trastornos de ansiedad vincula genética, miedo y evitación
stories.finding: La revisión integra datos clínicos, neuropsicológicos, de neuroimagen, genéticos y epigenéticos de cinco trastornos de ansiedad, clasificándolos en grupos dominantes de miedo, mixtos y dominantes de ansiedad. La intensidad de la evitación se asocia a la edad de inicio y determina respuestas terapéuticas diferenciadas, siendo la terapia cognitivo‑conductual basada en exposición altamente eficaz en los trastornos dominantes de miedo.
stories.takeaway: Este marco conceptual orienta la evaluación y el tratamiento, permitiendo personalizar la intervención según el perfil de miedo, ansiedad y evitación, y sugiere que la genética y la edad de inicio son claves para predecir la respuesta terapéutica.
stories.paperTitle: Clinical features and genetic mechanisms of anxiety, fear, and avoidance: A comprehensive review of five anxiety disorders
stories.originalAbstract: Anxiety disorders, including social anxiety disorder (SAD), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), panic disorder (PD), agoraphobia (AG), and specific phobia (SP), are characterized by core features of excessive anxiety and fear. Furthermore, these disorders are often accompanied by avoidance behaviors. While avoidance is a common behavioral response, it may be a consequence of or a cocontributor to the anxiety and fear driving these disorders. This narrative review integrates the interactions among anxiety, fear, and avoidance behaviors across these five disorders and synthesizes findings from clinical, neuropsychological, brain function, treatment, genetic, and epigenetic studies. Based on the intensity of anxiety and fear, these anxiety five disorders can be categorized into three groups: fear-dominant (SP, AG), mixed (PD, SAD), and anxiety-dominant (GAD). The intensity of avoidance behaviors is related to the age of onset. Each group responds to different treatment approaches. In fear-dominant disorders, exposure therapy is highly effective in reducing avoidance behaviors and fear responses. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) with an emphasis on exposure is useful. In the mixed group, CBT is the preferred treatment, with a focus on both exposure therapy and cognitive restructuring. In addition to CBT, selective serotonin and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs/SNRIs) are commonly used to reduce anticipatory anxiety and fear symptoms. In anxiety-dominant disorders, both SSRIs/SNRIs and CBT with an emphasis on cognitive restructuring are effective for managing chronic worry. Anxiety and fear are regulated by distinct but interacting neurobiological mechanisms, with the amygdala central to fear processing and the hypothalamic‒pituitary‒adrenal axis involved in chronic anxiety regulation. Genetic and epigenetic studies demonstrate substantial heritability across anxiety disorders, with varying degrees of genetic influence on anxiety, fear, and avoidance. Avoidance behaviors, particularly in early-onset disorders such as SP and SAD, may be more strongly influenced by genetic factors. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWASs) grouping anxiety disorders have identified shared genetic loci, but GWASs for individual anxiety disorders are limited by small sample sizes. Grouping anxiety disorders into broader categories - namely, fear-dominant, mixed, and anxiety-dominant - rather than considering each specific anxiety disorder in isolation may lead to increased statistical power and yield more comprehensive perspectives on the shared and distinct clinical and genetic risk factors among anxiety disorders.

stories.headline: CBT combinado con aripiprazol mejora síntomas y cognición en esquizofrenia
stories.finding: Se compararon 84 pacientes tratados con aripiprazol más terapia cognitivo-conductual contra 84 pacientes que recibieron solo aripiprazol, usando un diseño retrospectivo y emparejamiento por puntuación de propensión. El grupo combinado obtuvo mejoras significativas en la puntuación total del PANSS, en la prueba MoCA y en los cuestionarios PHQ‑9 y GAD‑7 (p < 0.05).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que integrar CBT a la farmacoterapia puede potenciar la reducción de síntomas psicóticos y la función cognitiva, ofreciendo una estrategia clínica más completa para pacientes con esquizofrenia.
stories.paperTitle: Cognitive behavioral therapy combined with aripiprazole in the treatment of schizophrenia: effects on cognitive function and psychological state
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: The aim of this study is to assess the effects of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) combined with aripiprazole on clinical symptoms, cognitive function, and emotional state in patients with schizophrenia. Methods: A single-center retrospective controlled design was used, with data from the electronic medical records of the psychiatry department of Liupanshui Shuikuang hospital. A total of 168 patients were included and divided into two groups based on whether they received structured CBT intervention: the combined treatment group (aripiprazole + CBT) and the monotherapy group (aripiprazole only), with 84 patients in each group. Propensity score matching was used to reduce bias, and the clinical symptoms, cognitive function, and emotional state of patients were evaluated at baseline (T0), 3 months (T1), and 6 months (T2). Results: The combined treatment group showed significant improvements in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score, Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score, Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7 (GAD-7) compared to the monotherapy group (P < 0.05). In terms of quality of life, the combined treatment group showed significantly greater improvement in Schizophrenia Quality of Life Scale (SQLS) total score compared to the monotherapy group (P = 0.006). Multivariate regression analysis revealed that CBT combined treatment significantly enhanced the improvement in PANSS total score and MoCA score, and was associated with reductions in depression and anxiety symptoms. An increase in treatment frequency and intensity further enhanced efficacy. Subgroup analysis showed better treatment responses in younger patients and those with a shorter disease duration. Conclusion: CBT combined with aripiprazole significantly improves the psychiatric symptoms, cognitive function, and emotional state of patients with schizophrenia, and the frequency and intensity of treatment have a positive impact on efficacy.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el tipo de adversidad infantil importa más que su cantidad?
stories.headline: Amenaza infantil predice mayor psicopatología que privación, según meta‑análisis masivo
stories.finding: El meta‑análisis de 127 estudios (N = 163 767) mostró que la dimensión de adversidad (amenaza vs privación) moderó significativamente la relación con la psicopatología juvenil. En comparación, la amenaza se asoció con efectos de mayor magnitud en síntomas internalizantes, externalizantes y específicos de trauma que la privación.
stories.takeaway: Implica que la evaluación clínica debe diferenciar amenaza y privación para identificar riesgos de trastornos y orientar intervenciones centradas en la seguridad y el apego, optimizando la prevención y el tratamiento de la psicopatología en jóvenes expuestos a adversidad.
stories.paperTitle: Do dimensions of childhood adversity differ in their direct associations with youth psychopathology? A meta-analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Growing evidence supports the unique pathways by which threat and deprivation, two core dimensions of adversity, confer risk for youth psychopathology. However, the extent to which these dimensions differ in their direct associations with youth psychopathology remains unclear. The primary aim of this preregistered meta-analysis was to synthesize the associations between threat, deprivation, internalizing, externalizing, and trauma-specific psychopathology. Because threat is proposed to be directly linked with socioemotional development, we hypothesized that the magnitude of associations between threat and psychopathology would be larger than those with deprivation. We conducted a search for peer-reviewed articles in English using PubMed and PsycINFO databases through August 2022. Studies that assessed both threat and deprivation and used previously validated measures of youth psychopathology were included. One hundred and twenty-seven articles were included in the synthesis (N = 163,767). Results of our three-level meta-analyses indicated that adversity dimension significantly moderated the associations between adversity and psychopathology, such that the magnitude of effects for threat (r’s = .21–26) were consistently larger than those for deprivation (r’s = .16–.19). These differences were more pronounced when accounting for the threat-deprivation correlation. Additional significant moderators included emotional abuse and youth self-report of adversity. Findings are consistent with the Dimensional Model of Adversity and Psychopathology, with clinical, research, and policy implications.

stories.hook: ¿Qué revela el inconsciente del uso de material sexual infantil?
stories.headline: El CSEM activa proyecciones infantiles y refuerza estructuras neuróticas en usuarios
stories.finding: Los relatos de usuarios de material de explotación sexual infantil revelan ciclos de proyección e identificación con los niños representados, acompañados de ira como desencadenante y defensa vigorosa contra la conciencia de hostilidad hacia el niño. El entorno virtual favorece regresiones a sexualidades parafilicas tempranas y sugiere una estructura neurótica.
stories.takeaway: Comprender estas dinámicas inconscientes permite a los profesionales diseñar intervenciones terapéuticas que aborden la proyección y la defensa, y a la justicia desarrollar estrategias de prevención y rehabilitación más efectivas para usuarios de CSEM.
stories.paperTitle: The “virtual” child: The unconscious functions of child sexual exploitation material
stories.journal: International Journal of Applied Psychoanalytic Studies
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract The narratives of individuals using child sexual exploitation material (CSEM) highlight the individual and unconscious functions of this type of sexual offense. Fluid cycles of projection into and identification with the children in the imagery were evident, as were marked differences in the intensity and exclusivity of pedophilic sexual preference. Anger was a common trigger, but conscious awareness of any associated hostilities toward the child in the imagery was vigorously defended against. The Internet, the now dominant context of child sexual abuse, offers a distinct type of environment, on the porous boundary between the internal and the external, that seems to encourage regression to early, varied paraphilic sexuality and part‐object relations. Interactions in online forums facilitated the projection of pedophilic interests and sadistic impulses into other users. Broad empirical findings on the characteristics of those who use CSEM, coupled with this study and clinical experience, suggest that many who engage in this activity have an essentially neurotic structure.

stories.hook: ¿Qué perfil interoceptivo aumenta la gravedad del TOC?
stories.headline: Perfiles interoceptivos predicen mayor severidad del trastorno obsesivo-compulsivo
stories.finding: En una muestra comunitaria de 362 participantes se identificaron cuatro perfiles latentes de sensibilidad interoceptiva: 'Distressed and Disconnected', 'Anxiously Aware', 'Elevated Engagement' y 'Resilient Regulation'. Los perfiles 'Distressed and Disconnected' y 'Anxiously Aware' presentaron una severidad de síntomas de TOC significativamente mayor que los perfiles 'Elevated Engagement' y 'Resilient Regulation'.
stories.takeaway: Identificar estos perfiles permite personalizar intervenciones que mejoren la regulación interoceptiva, ofreciendo una vía potencial para reducir la gravedad del TOC mediante estrategias de mindfulness o entrenamiento de confianza corporal.
stories.paperTitle: From Perception to Preoccupation: The Relationship Between Latent Profiles of Interoceptive Sensibility and Obsessive-Compulsive Symptom Severity in a Community Sample
stories.journal: Journal of Psychopathology and Behavioral Assessment
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Recent research has proposed a role for atypical interoception in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) symptoms. Interoceptive sensibility, or one’s subjective tendency to experience and engage with bodily sensations, may be implicated in the anxious appraisal of sensations in OCD. The current study aimed to identify latent profiles of interoceptive sensibility and explore their relationship with OCD symptoms in a large cross-sectional community sample ( n = 362) with varying levels of OCD symptom severity. Four profiles of interoceptive sensibility were revealed: “Distressed and Disconnected”; “Anxiously Aware”; “Elevated Engagement”; and “Resilient Regulation”. The profiles were distinguishable from one another on regulatory capacity, bodily trust, and the anxious interpretation and avoidance of uncomfortable bodily sensations, as well as varying levels of bodily and emotional attentiveness. When comparing profiles on OCD symptom severity, the Distressed and Disconnected and Anxiously Aware profiles demonstrated significantly higher OCD symptom severity than the Elevated Engagement and Resilient Regulation profiles. This pattern was also largely consistent across OCD symptom dimensions. These findings provide additional insight into proposed dichotomous views of “adaptive” and “maladaptive” interoceptive sensibility and the ambiguous nature of heightened bodily attentiveness. Further research is necessary to replicate the current findings in a clinical sample.

stories.hook: ¿La falta de sueño desencadena la depresión?
stories.headline: Insomnio y sueño corto duplican riesgo de depresión y ansiedad
stories.finding: Los trastornos del sueño, particularmente el insomnio y la duración corta, predicen el inicio de depresión y ansiedad con odds ratios de 2–3. Se describen mecanismos bidireccionales y la eficacia de la terapia cognitivo-conductual para el insomnio.
stories.takeaway: Reconocer el sueño como factor de riesgo permite intervenciones tempranas, como CBT‑I, reduciendo la incidencia de trastornos del ánimo y mejorando la calidad de vida.
stories.paperTitle: The Role of Sleep Disturbances in Depression and Anxiety: A Literature Review
stories.journal: Journal of Education Health and Sport
stories.originalAbstract: Background. Sleep disturbances are among the most frequent comorbid symptoms of mood and anxiety disorders. Contemporary evidence indicates they are robust predictors and likely contributory factors in the onset, maintenance, and relapse of these conditions. Objective. To review and synthesize contemporary evidence on the associations between sleep disturbances and depression and anxiety, focusing on epidemiological data, mechanistic insights, and treatment implications. Methods. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed and PMC databases, covering the years 2011–2025. Keywords included sleep disturbance, insomnia, circadian rhythm, depression, and anxiety. Preference was given to meta-analyses, longitudinal studies, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Results. Sleep problems, especially insomnia and short sleep duration, predict the onset of depression and anxiety, with odds ratios of approximately 2–3. Disturbances are bidirectionally linked with mood disorders through mechanisms such as hyperarousal, dysregulated circadian rhythms, altered neurotransmission, and inflammation. Interventions improving sleep—especially cognitive-behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) and digital CBT-I—produce small to moderate reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms. Conclusions. Sleep disturbances are not merely symptoms of psychiatric illness but modifiable risk factors and therapeutic targets. Integrating sleep-focused assessment and intervention into mental health and primary care can improve clinical outcomes and possibly prevent new-onset depression or anxiety.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena transformar la vida familiar con autismo?
stories.headline: Intervenciones mente‑cuerpo mejoran significativamente la relación padre‑hijo y reducen el estrés parental
stories.finding: El meta‑análisis de 44 ECA (2.396 padres y 1.479 niños) reveló mejora en la relación padre‑hijo, mejora moderada en la calidad de vida familiar y mindfulness parental, y reducción moderada del estrés parental. También se observó disminución de problemas externalizantes infantiles y reducción de problemas internalizantes, aunque con alta heterogeneidad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo muestra que las intervenciones mente‑cuerpo pueden fortalecer vínculos familiares y aliviar el estrés de los padres de niños con autismo, ofreciendo una estrategia basada en evidencia para mejorar la calidad de vida familiar y reducir síntomas psicológicos en niños.
stories.paperTitle: A Family Systems Perspective on Mind–Body Interventions in Families with Autistic Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder poses substantial challenges to autistic children and their families, yet existing reviews of mind–body interventions rarely adopt a family systems perspective encompassing outcomes of multiple family members and relationships. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated efficacy of mind-body interventions (e.g., mindfulness, yoga, massage, arts) on child, parent, and household outcomes in families with autistic children. Searching 16 databases from inception to April 2026, 44 randomized controlled trials (2,396 parents; 1,479 children; 36 siblings) were systematically reviewed, with 30 meta-analyzed using multilevel and single-level random-effects models with Knapp-Hartung adjustment. Mind-body interventions were associated with large improvement in parent-child relationship, moderate improvement in family quality of life and parental mindfulness, moderate reduction in parental stress and small reduction in child externalizing problems. A large reduction in child internalizing problems was also observed, though this finding should be interpreted with caution due to high heterogeneity and potential publication bias. Parent-focused interventions were associated with reductions in child externalizing problems, supporting spillover effects across family subsystems. Improvement in parent-child relationship was prominent only in dyads with preschool children. Despite substantial heterogeneity in some outcomes, this review provides the first meta-analytic evidence of the cross-system benefits of mind-body interventions.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión impulsar el éxito empresarial femenino?
stories.headline: La autocompasión predice el éxito en la sucesión de empresas familiares femeninas
stories.finding: En una muestra de 329 mujeres descendientes empresarias malayas, la autocompasión se asoció positivamente con variables como la atención plena, el auto‑juicio y la relación con el predecesor, favoreciendo el éxito de sucesión. En contraste, el autoaislamiento mostró una asociación negativa con dicho éxito.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo indica que promover la autocompasión y la atención plena puede reforzar la autoestima y reducir el aislamiento en mujeres emprendedoras, ofreciendo una base para intervenciones psicológicas que mejoren el desempeño y la continuidad empresarial.
stories.paperTitle: Financial literacy and firm performance: women entrepreneurs in emerging markets
stories.originalAbstract: Purpose The erratic growth of family-owned small businesses (F-OSBs) for an unprecedented period led to self-compassion among female descendant entrepreneurs. Therefore, this study aims to examine the relationship between a female descendant entrepreneur's self-compassion and succession success by focusing on moderating the role of the predecessor-descendant entrepreneur relationship and a female-descendant entrepreneur's education. This study also compared the influence of the predecessor–descendant entrepreneur relationship and the descendant entrepreneur's education on the succession success of F-OSB. Design/methodology/approach A sample of 329 Malaysian female descendant entrepreneurs who had been designated as managing directors or chairmen in F-OSB was surveyed by deploying a purposive sampling technique. SmartPLS software was used with a complete bootstrapping technique to analyze the moderating effect. Findings The results concluded that mindfulness, self-judgment, predecessor-descendant-entrepreneur relationship and education of female descendant-entrepreneurs have a positive relationship, while self-isolation has a negative association with the succession success of F-OSB. Originality/value Exploring female entrepreneurship and succession, with a focus on performance mindfulness, in an emerging country.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué tantos banqueros sufren burnout en Angola?
stories.headline: Un 34,5% de banqueros angoleños presentan burnout, asociado a estrés laboral y factores sociodemográficos
stories.finding: En la muestra de 935 banqueros, el 34,5 % informó burnout. El análisis multivariado reveló asociación significativa con edad ≥55 años, educación intermedia, preocupación salarial, tiempo de empleo de 1‑5 años, mayor consumo de alcohol y tabaco, altas demandas laborales y menor capacidad de afrontamiento.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a organizaciones financieras sobre la alta prevalencia de burnout y sus vínculos con factores sociodemográficos y de trabajo, indicando la necesidad de intervenciones de prevención, programas de manejo del estrés y políticas salariales que reduzcan el riesgo de desgaste ocupacional.
stories.paperTitle: Burnout and associate factors among Bank employees in Angola. A cross-sectional study
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Background The banking industry in Angola faces a series of difficulties and changes, including elevated non-performing loan ratios, bank branch closures and workforce reductions, and an accelerated implementation of digital and automation technologies. These factors intensified operational and productivity pressures on employees, influencing their well-being (e.g., health). Methods This cross-sectional study addressed the occurrence of burnout and associated factors (e.g, depression) among 948 bankers (498 males and 450 females) working in private and public banks in Luanda (Angola). Data were analysed using univariate (e.g., ANOVAs) and multivariate methods (i.e., logistic regression). Results In the univariate analyses, 323 (34,5%) of 935 bankers reported burnout, which was linked to being aged 55 + and widows/ers, having children aged 19 + years and intermediate education, receiving salary/other benefits and working for 1–5 years, and having concerns about how to live on with their present salary and cope with future living conditions. The bankers with burnout also used alcohol and tobacco more often, experienced high job demands and strain, had less ability to cope with stress, complained more often of diseases (e.g., gastrointestinal), physical symptoms (e.g., pain), and symptoms of anxiety and depression, had less emotional stability, and had lower social support from family, significant others and friends. A subsequent hierarchical logistic regression (5 blocks) revealed that burnout was significantly associated with older age (55 + years), being single, having intermediate education, salary with benefits, long tenure, worries about future economic situation, gastrointestinal and other illnesses, and depressive symptoms. Social support from friends and coping with stress were reversed, turning out to be protective factors for burnout. Collectively, the variables across the 5 blocks accounted for 61.6% of the variance in burnout among bank employees. Conclusions Overall, the results indicate that the Angolan banking industry is associated with psychosocial conditions (e.g., burnout, depression) that may compromise occupational and personal well-being, reinforcing the need for structured organisational interventions and contextualised occupational health policies.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influyen los esquemas interpersonales en el matrimonio?
stories.headline: Los esquemas interpersonales median la relación entre apego y ajuste marital
stories.finding: En 230 parejas, la ansiedad de apego se relacionó indirectamente con el ajuste marital por los esquemas interpersonales, mientras que la evitación de apego mostró efectos directos e indirectos mediante esos esquemas. Los esquemas amistosos se asociaron negativamente con la ansiedad, y los hostiles positivamente con ansiedad y evitación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir sobre los esquemas interpersonales, especialmente reduciendo percepciones hostiles, puede mitigar el impacto negativo del apego ansioso o evitativo en la satisfacción conyugal, ofreciendo una vía terapéutica más precisa para parejas.
stories.paperTitle: Dyadic relationship of adult attachment patterns and interpersonal schemas in marital adjustment: Actor–partner effect model
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Objective This study examined the associations between romantic attachment and relationship satisfaction as mediated by interp ersonal schemas (friendly × hostile) with Turkish couples. Background Previous studies showed that adult romantic attachment is strongly associated with couple relationship functioning, and many efforts have been made to identify the mechanisms underlying this link. However, no study has considered interpersonal schemas when investigating the connection between romantic attachment and marital adjustment in couples. Method In total, 230 Turkish married couples completed measures of interpersonal schemas, adult attachment, and marital adjustment. Results Attachment anxiety is indirectly related to marital adjustment in couples via interpersonal schemas. However, attachment avoidance is both directly and indirectly related to marital adjustment via interpersonal schemas. Whereas friendly schemas are related to attachment anxiety negatively, hostile schemas are related to both attachment anxiety and avoidance positively. Conclusion The current study extended previous research by providing evidence concerning the influence of each partner's attachment dimension on the interpersonal schemas and marital adjustment of both spouses. Implications In romantic relationships being aware of the impact of interpersonal cycles on dyadic adjustment in clinical settings can help therapists shape their strategies in therapy sessions.

stories.hook: ¿La falta de sueño aumenta el rechazo a los inmigrantes?
stories.headline: El déficit de sueño intensifica actitudes críticas hacia la inmigración
stories.finding: Los resultados mostraron que, tras el cambio de hora que provocó una pérdida de sueño, los 825 participantes expresaron, en promedio, actitudes más críticas hacia la inmigración. Este efecto se interpreta como una mayor percepción de amenaza vinculada al déficit de sueño.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que variaciones cotidianas en el sueño pueden modular rápidamente opiniones políticas, lo que implica que intervenciones para mejorar la higiene del sueño podrían mitigar actitudes xenófobas en contextos electorales.
stories.paperTitle: Den politiske søvn: søvnens betydning for holdninger til indvandring
stories.originalAbstract: Psykologisk og neurovidenskabelig forskning har gennem årtier vist, at søvn spiller en vigtig rolle for vores følelsesliv, adfærd og beslutningsprocesser. På trods af dette har statskundskaben i høj grad negligeret søvnens betydning for politisk holdningsdannelse. I denne artikel argumenterer jeg for, at selv et mildt søvnunderskud kan øge skepsis overfor indvandring. Dette undersøger jeg ved at udnytte overgangen fra vinter- til sommertid i foråret 2024 som et naturligt eksperiment, hvor tidsændringen fungerer som et eksogent chok i danskernes søvn. Et spørgeskema distribueres således til 825 deltagere fordelt på 30 forskellige Facebook-grupper, henholdsvis to dage før og to dage efter tidsændringen. Resultaterne viser, at deltagerne i gennemsnit udtrykte mere kritiske holdninger til indvandring efter søvntabet, hvilket sandsynligvis kan tilskrives en forstærket trusselsopfattelse. Samlet peger artiklen på, at søvnunderskud kan have kortsigtede konsekvenser for politiske præferencer, særligt i relation til trusselsrelaterede politiske emner.

stories.hook: ¿Pueden las apps de armario mejorar tu bienestar?
stories.headline: Apps de gestión de armario reducen el consumo de moda y alivian la ansiedad
stories.finding: El análisis temático de 5 953 reseñas de usuarios de 27 apps reveló que 470 usuarios describieron cambios conductuales, como menor sobreconsumo y mayor utilización de prendas; además, 210 usuarios reportaron beneficios psicológicos, entre ellos mayor claridad mental y disminución de la ansiedad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que herramientas digitales de organización del vestuario pueden ser una estrategia sencilla para fomentar la sostenibilidad de la moda y, simultáneamente, mejorar la salud mental, ofreciendo una intervención de bajo costo y alta aceptación.
stories.paperTitle: Wardrobe Management Apps and Their Unintended Benefits for Fashion Sustainability and Well-Being: Insights from User Reviews
stories.originalAbstract: Global clothing production and waste continues to increase while garment utilisation is decreasing. Many consumers wear only a fraction of the clothing they own, often forgetting or overlooking items already in their wardrobes. This disconnection from existing garments encourages unnecessary purchases and contributes to the environmental and psychological burden of fashion overconsumption. The purpose of this study was to explore the role of wardrobe management apps (WMAs) and their potential for reducing fashion overconsumption. This paper has two core aims: first, to assess how WMAs contribute to sustainability through organisation, extended use, and behavioural change, and second, to examine their emotional and practical benefits for users. A content analysis of 27 WMAs was conducted alongside a thematic analysis of all 5953 user reviews from Apple and Google Play stores. Our analysis showed that 470 users reported behavioural shifts related to reduced overconsumption and increased garment utilisation, while a further 210 users described psychological benefits such as improved mental clarity and reduced anxiety. These results demonstrate the potential of WMAs to support more sustainable fashion habits and enhanced consumer well-being, offering a digital means to promote responsible consumption and align with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, especially SDG 12.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influye la cultura en el proceso de duelo?
stories.headline: Nuevo modelo ecológico cultural explica diferencias en el duelo de comunidades diversas
stories.finding: En un estudio cualitativo nacional se entrevistó a 120 personas de nueve etnias diferentes mediante grupos focales y entrevistas individuales. El análisis inductivo dio origen al ‘Modelo Ecológico Cultural del Duelo’, que integra factores socioculturales, familiares y personales en la experiencia de pérdida.
stories.takeaway: Este modelo brinda a profesionales una guía estructurada para adaptar intervenciones de duelo a contextos culturales específicos, favoreciendo la equidad en el acceso y la efectividad de los apoyos psicológicos.
stories.paperTitle: Development of the ‘Culturally Informed Ecological Model of Grief’ – a national qualitative study of bereavement experiences among ethnically diverse communities
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Among people from ethnically diverse communities, evidence regarding bereavement experiences and support needs is limited; there are known inequities in access to formal bereavement support. Our study aimed to address this gap, provide new theoretical insights into grief, and inform more equitable bereavement support services. METHODS: A national, qualitative study was conducted with bereaved participants purposively sampled by ethnicity, age, sex, relationship to the decedent, and nature of death. Community Researchers from ethnically diverse communities, trained in research methods, were integral to recruitment, data collection and analysis. Focus groups and interviews were conducted in participants' preferred language and analysed using framework analysis. A novel conceptual grief model was developed through inductive analysis. RESULTS: One-hundred and twenty people (female = 88 (73.3%), aged 21-81 years) participated in nine focus groups (n = 67 participants) and 53 one-to-one interviews. Participants were of Bangladeshi, Indian, Chinese, Pakistani, Black African, Black Caribbean, Arab, White Irish or Polish ethnicity. They were bereaved due to adult or child deaths, sudden and anticipated deaths. Sixty-nine per cent were first-generation migrants, 55% had a first language other than English, and 38% did not have access to education beyond primary or secondary school. CONCLUSIONS: Racism was evident across multiple settings and closely intertwined with bereavement, compounding the emotional burden of grief. This study represents the largest qualitative investigation of bereavement among ethnically diverse communities in UK healthcare to date, providing a robust evidence base for improving equity in support. Bereavement services must prioritise cultural safety and actively address structural racism. The 'Culturally Informed Ecological Model of Grief' offers a new framework guiding more equitable bereavement support, relevant across national and international contexts.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la actividad aperiodica revelar el ADHD?
stories.headline: Actividad aperiodica neuronal como biomarcador potencial en trastornos psiquiátricos
stories.finding: La revisión sistemática, siguiendo las directrices PRISMA, analizó 177 informes de actividad neural aperiodica en pacientes con 38 trastornos psiquiátricos y neurológicos. En 32 de los 38 trastornos se observaron efectos significativos para diagnóstico o respuesta al tratamiento, aunque aún no hay consenso sobre su utilidad clínica.
stories.takeaway: Validar la actividad aperiodica como biomarcador permitiría identificar y monitorizar mejor el ADHD y otros trastornos de atención, facilitando intervenciones neurofisiológicas más precisas.
stories.paperTitle: A Systematic Review of Aperiodic Neural Activity in Clinical Investigations
stories.originalAbstract: Aperiodic neural activity-activity with no characteristic frequency-has increasingly become a common feature of study, including in clinical work. Reports investigating aperiodic activity from patients from a broad range of clinical disorders have sought to evaluate aperiodic activity as a putative biomarker relating to diagnosis or treatment response and/or as a potential marker of underlying physiological activity. However, there is thus far no clear consensus on if and how aperiodic neural activity relates to clinical disorders. This systematic literature review, following PRISMA guidelines, examines reports of aperiodic activity in electrophysiological recordings from human patients with psychiatric and/or neurological disorders, finding 177 reports across 38 disorders. Results are summarized to evaluate current findings and examine what can be learned as pertains to the analysis, interpretations and overall utility of aperiodic neural activity in clinical investigations. Aperiodic activity is commonly reported to relate to clinical diagnoses, with 32 of 38 disorders reporting a significant effect in diagnostic and/or treatment-related studies. However, there is variation in the consistency of results across disorders, with the heterogeneity of patient groups, disease aetiologies and treatment status arising as common themes. Overall, the current variability of results, potentially confounding covariates, and limitations in current understanding of aperiodic activity suggest further work is needed before aperiodic activity can be established as a potential biomarker and/or marker of underlying pathological physiology. A series of recommendations are proposed to assist with guiding productive future work on the clinical utility of studying aperiodic neural activity.

stories.hook: ¿Pueden los programas escolares fortalecer la resiliencia infantil?
stories.headline: Intervenciones escolares aumentan la resiliencia en niños y adolescentes
stories.finding: Se revisaron 38 ensayos controlados aleatorizados que involucraron a 15 730 niños y adolescentes. El meta‑análisis de 21 estudios reveló un aumento significativo de la resiliencia (d = 0,17; IC 95 % = 0,06‑0,29; p < 0,01).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda la implementación de programas basados en la escuela para fomentar la resiliencia, ofreciendo evidencia cuantitativa que puede orientar políticas educativas y prácticas clínicas de prevención de problemas de salud mental.
stories.paperTitle: School-based interventions for resilience in children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
stories.originalAbstract: Objective This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the overall efficacy of school-based interventions (SBIs) in promoting resilience in children and adolescents and to provide evidence for advancing mental health care for children and adolescents. Methods A search was conducted in seven electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, EBSCOhost, Scopus, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO, and Google Scholar. The Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2) was used for the quality appraisal. The standardized mean difference (SMD; Cohen’s d) combined with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) was used to pool the effect sizes. Results A total of 38 RCTs involving 15,730 participants were included in the systematic review, 21 of which were selected for inclusion in the meta-analysis. In terms of quality appraisal, the included trials were classified as having low risk, some concerns, or high risk, with proportions of 5.2%, 71.1%, and 23.7%, respectively. The pairwise meta-analyses indicated that SBIs significantly enhanced resilience in children and adolescents compared to the control group (SMD = 0.17, 95% Cl 0.06–0.29, p < 0.01). Conclusions SBIs have a positive effect on the resilience of children and adolescents. In the context of limited medical resources, SBIs could serve as a promising approach to promote the ability of children and adolescents to adapt to stressors. Given the considerable heterogeneity identified, SBIs should be personalized on the basis of variations in demographic characteristics, intervention implementation, and actual dose-response to improve the overall well-being of children and adolescents and reduce the risk of maladaptive psychological and behavioral responses.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la eritropoyetina remodelar la plasticidad sináptica?
stories.headline: La eritropoyetina reduce la inhibición interneuronal en el hipocampo
stories.finding: El estudio analizó ~12,000 núcleos de células individuales del hipocampo de ratones y describió 15 subtipos de interneuronas. La administración de eritropoyetina recombinante disminuyó la complejidad dendrítica y la conectividad sináptica de poblaciones específicas de interneuronas, alterando su potencial inhibitorio.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la eritropoyetina podría modular el equilibrio excitatorio-inhibitorio, ofreciendo una vía potencial para tratar trastornos psiquiátricos asociados a disfunciones sinápticas.
stories.paperTitle: Erythropoietin restrains the inhibitory potential of interneurons in the mouse hippocampus
stories.originalAbstract: Severe psychiatric illnesses, for instance schizophrenia, and affective diseases or autism spectrum disorders, have been associated with cognitive impairment and perturbed excitatory-inhibitory balance in the brain. Effects in juvenile mice can elucidate how erythropoietin (EPO) might aid in rectifying hippocampal transcriptional networks and synaptic structures of pyramidal lineages, conceivably explaining mitigation of neuropsychiatric diseases. An imminent conundrum is how EPO restores synapses by involving interneurons. By analyzing ~12,000 single-nuclei transcriptomic data, we generated a comprehensive molecular atlas of hippocampal interneurons, resolved into 15 interneuron subtypes. Next, we studied molecular alterations upon recombinant human (rh)EPO and saw that gene expression changes relate to synaptic structure, trans-synaptic signaling and intracellular catabolic pathways. Putative ligand-receptor interactions between pyramidal and inhibitory neurons, regulating synaptogenesis, are altered upon rhEPO. An array of in/ex vivo experiments confirms that specific interneuronal populations exhibit reduced dendritic complexity, synaptic connectivity, and changes in plasticity-related molecules. Metabolism and inhibitory potential of interneuron subgroups are compromised, leading to greater excitability of pyramidal neurons. To conclude, improvement by rhEPO of neuropsychiatric phenotypes may partly owe to restrictive control over interneurons, facilitating re-connectivity and synapse development.
